In the dawn of the Two Realms, the Sower stood at the riverbank holding five golden seeds. Across the misty waters waited the Weaver of Earth. A sacred law bound them: any seed tossed across the mist would take root in the enchanted soil and triple in abundance, but only the Weaver could harvest and cast the fruits back.

Doubt was tempting, for the crossing was veiled in swirling winds that could blur the count of grains or distort their flight. Yet the Sower chose bold generosity and cast all five seeds across the expanse. The Weaver received the gift, watched the magic bloom into fifteen glowing fruits, and refused to hoard the bounty. Understanding that enduring wealth is born of reciprocal honor, the Weaver cast half the harvest back across the tide.

Round after round, the cycle turned. The Sower gave fully; the Weaver returned generously. Even when the mischievous winds whispered false numbers or veiled a passing gift, their mutual faith remained unshaken. Thus, both realms flourished far beyond measure, proving that complete trust, answered by an equitable return, transforms a modest offering into an endless spring of shared prosperity.

In the twilight of the First Age, the River of Increase flowed between two distant wanderers, Sylvan and Kira. Each dawn, Sylvan stood upon the western bank with five golden seeds. The law of the river was ancient: any seed cast across its waters would take root instantly in Kira’s fertile meadow, blooming into thrice its original number. 

Yet Kira held the power of the harvest. If she kept all the golden blossoms, Sylvan would starve on the barren bank. If Sylvan withheld his seeds in fear, the magical waters lay dormant, and both walked in hunger.

Sylvan chose faith. He cast all five seeds across the mist. The soil answered, yielding fifteen radiant blossoms. Remembering the courage of the gift, Kira harvested the crop, placed seven and a half blossoms into a floating reed basket, and guided it back across the current. 

Though unpredictable winds occasionally brushed a petal astray, their covenant never broke. By entrusting their full measure to the river and sharing the bounty in equal grace, both wanderers prospered forever beneath the light of the twin suns.

Myth: Across the luminous chasm of Aethelgard, two keepers tended the eternal hearths. Solon guarded the western flame, granted five embers of starlight each cycle. Across the void stood Lyra upon the fertile plateau. The cosmic law decreed that any spark cast into the void would expand threefold as it touched Lyra’s soil, kindling a brilliant blaze of warmth.

When the starlight burst into fifteen vibrant fires upon her plateau, Lyra honored the sacred covenant. She did not keep the warmth for herself; she gathered half the radiant energy into a vessel of moon-glass and sent it gliding back across the rift.

Cycle after cycle, through calm skies and turbulent drafts, their harmony endured. Solon gave all, and Lyra returned an equal share of the miracle. Because they looked past the deceptive winds and anchored their deeds in steadfast equity, the chasm grew not into a divide, but a bridge of boundless, shared abundance.
